items.title: JKK Wiki
items.text:
Welcome to the JKK wiki! Here you can find information about our research, projects, and publications.

Welcome to JKK wiki

Technical documentation for JKK's autonomous vehicle research platforms (hardware specs, our ROS 2 software stack, and datasets) covering the vehicles, robots, and test infrastructure at Győr Campus and ZalaZone. Written for lab members, students, and research partners working directly with our systems.

Looking for our research mission or publication list instead? See Home or Publications.

Hardware

Sensor and vehicle specifications for our research platforms: ground vehicle sensor sets, GNSS/LiDAR/radar/camera/IMU datasheets, and actuation (PACMod, LabVIEW).

Software

Our ROS 2 stack: sensor drivers, networking/QoS, localization, Autoware integration, HD maps, and lab utilities.

Datasets

Recorded rosbag/mcap logs and HLB use-case data from our vehicles, released for research and teaching.

Full dataset catalog

Contributing

Found an error or a missing page? Edit this wiki on GitHub.

items.title: 2026.L PacMOD ROS2
items.text:
Communtations with vehicle happens through /pacmod topics, using the vehicles CAN bus network.

Within the Spectra PC we have a Kvaser PCIEcan 4xHS card that supports native communication through the can bus. Currently we' using the default Linux SocketCAN to acess the device, and the connected CAN-bus, on the can0 channel.

To start the ROS2 driver:

ros2 launch lexus_bringup can_and_status.launch.py

To see all to CAN channels on the PC: 

sudo ifconfig -a

To restart the SocketCAN on the pc 

sudo ip link set can0 down
sudo ip link set can0 up

items.title: Ouster ROS 2 driver
items.text:
This page is a practical quick start for the official Ouster ROS 2 driver from ouster-lidar/ouster-ros. It focuses on the workflow we use most often: prepare a ROS 2 workspace, build the driver, and launch a live sensor.

For hardware background and model comparison, see the general Ouster overview in ouster.md.

items.title: What the driver does
items.text:
The ROS 2 driver connects to an Ouster sensor, configures it, and publishes the live data as ROS topics. The main outputs are:

  • /ouster/imu
  • /ouster/points
  • /ouster/points2 when the sensor is configured for dual return

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
The official ROS 2 branch targets Rolling, Humble, Iron, Jazzy, and Kilted. In practice, you should already have a working ROS 2 installation and a sourced workspace environment.

Install the common dependencies first:

sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    libeigen3-dev \
    libjsoncpp-dev \
    libspdlog-dev \
    libcurl4-openssl-dev \
    python3-colcon-common-extensions \
    ros-$ROS_DISTRO-pcl-ros \
    ros-$ROS_DISTRO-tf2-eigen \
    ros-$ROS_DISTRO-rviz2

If you plan to use PCAP replay later, also install libpcap-dev.

items.title: Clone and build
items.text:
Create a ROS 2 workspace and clone the ROS 2 branch of the driver into src:

mkdir -p ~/ros2_ws/src
cd ~/ros2_ws/src
git clone -b ros2 --recurse-submodules https://github.com/ouster-lidar/ouster-ros.git

Source your ROS 2 environment and build the workspace with colcon:

source /opt/ros/$ROS_DISTRO/setup.bash
cd ~/ros2_ws
colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
We currently use the lexus_bringup repository.

To launch all sensors and generate a merged point cloud, run:

ros2 launch lexus_bringup lidar_os_merged.launch.py

The sensor configuration files are located in lexus_bringup/config/lidar.

The Ouster sensor IP addresses are:

  • Ouster Center: 192.168.10.20
  • Ouster Left: 192.168.10.23
  • Ouster Right: 192.168.10.21
